subject: Variant gating proposal and emergency hold for model update
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Shaw <ellie@olivehealth.io>, procurement@olivehealth.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + recommended models / next steps after today's discovery

Hi Ellie / Olive team —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so there’s a single place to reference: 

What we heard
- Primary workload: patient triage summarization + follow-up recommendation (short clinical notes, variable prompts).
- Key constraints: sub-200ms median response target for triage step, tight safety constraints on hallucinations for medication mentions, and enterprise data retention requirements.

Initial recommendations (from the call)
- Model shortlist: redwood-phi-2-medium (baseline, quantized), redwood-stable-13b (higher-fidelity variant), redwood-lite-7b for low-cost batch jobs.
- Eval plan: run our prompt set against v1 (current in trial) and the new v2 variant; share benchmark CSV and prompt pack.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Marissa will send the eval pack and preliminary benchmarks for v1 vs v2 (we agreed to share raw prompts so you can eyeball failure modes).
2) We will put a conservative gating suggestion in writing if the v2 rollout shows regression on hallucination recall — the idea is a temporary variant hold (emergency hold) and a fallback to v1.
3) Procurement: please share a preferred PO cadence and any required security questionnaire reminders.

I’m copying Marissa who will attach the artifacts and a short runbook for a conservative pin/gating flow we use in these situations.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ellie Shaw <ellie@olivehealth.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@olivehealth.io
Date: 2026-11-29T10:05:00Z
Subject: Eval pack + benchmarks (v1 vs v2) + suggested conservative gating

Hi all —

Attached: 
- olive_benchmarks_v2_vs_v1.csv (summary rows + per-prompt diff)
- olive_prompt_set_v1.txt (the de-identified prompts we used)
- slo_comparison.drawio (visual of our suggested latency vs cost tradeoffs)

High-level takeaways from the run (short):
- Latency: v2 median is ~12% slower at your target sequence length (still within SLO with expected autoscaling, but headroom is smaller).
- Quality: for ~92% of prompts v2 is neutral/improved; for a focused subset (~8%) we observed hallucination-type failures where medication names were hallucinated or incorrectly asserted.
- Token cost: v2 is ~18% more expensive per token on average.

Suggested conservative gating (what we discussed):
- Canary 10% traffic to v2 for 48 hours with automatic rollback on key metric delta (hallucination FPR > 1.5x baseline or critical regressed examples in the watchlist).
- Emergency hold: immediately pin production route to v1 if we see 2 confirmed critical hallucinations in different patient cohorts.

I’m including two quick scripts in the runbook (in the Drive link below) that your engineers can use to pin a model at route-level and to snapshot slow tokens for triage.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/olivedrive-eval-pack
Eval run id: ev-2026-11-29-44 (results page: https://app.redwood.com/eval/runs/ev-2026-11-29-44)

Happy to walk through specific rows if you want — I can do a short call this afternoon.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: olive_benchmarks_v2_vs_v1.csv (CSV), olive_prompt_set_v1.txt (TXT), slo_comparison.drawio (DRAWIO)

From: Ellie Shaw <ellie@olivehealth.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@olivehealth.io
Date: 2026-11-29T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Eval pack + benchmarks (v1 vs v2) + suggested conservative gating

Thanks Priya / Marissa — helpful summary. Quick notes from our side after we skimmed the artifacts: 

- Appreciate the canary / gating approach. However, the examples in the CSV flagged a handful of critical failures that look real — I attached a zip with the de-identified failed_examples_ellie.zip so you can see the raw outputs vs expected.
- Our clinical safety lead asked: if v2 is auto-rolled and we see those hallucinations, how fast can we route back to v1? We need the rollback to be within the same minute (automated route pin).
- Procurement: we’re also flagging a requirement that any emergency hold must be executable without a signed SOW amendment (we will accept an operational rollback as part of the trial).

We’re open to a short runbook review call; availability: 2–4pm ET today.

— Ellie
Ellie Shaw
Head of Clinical Integrations, Olive Health
ellie@olivehealth.io

Attachment stub: failed_examples_ellie.zip

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Shaw <ellie@olivehealth.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@olivehealth.io
Date: 2026-11-29T12:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Variant gating proposal and emergency hold for model update

Ellie — thanks for the quick review and for sending the failed examples. I reviewed a sample and agree they are concerning. Proposed immediate steps so we’re aligned operationally: 

1) Emergency route hold: Redwood ops can enact a route-level pin to redwood-phi-2-medium (v1) in under 60s. We will provide the runbook and a 1-click script that your infra team can keep in the environment if you prefer local execution.
2) Canary plan: start with 5% traffic for 24 hours rather than 10%/48h given the failure footprint you observed.
3) Auto-rollback triggers (we will implement per your ask): 
   - Hallucination event count >= 2 distinct critical failures within 60 minutes, OR
   - Hallucination FPR > 1.5x baseline for the watchlist subset.
4) Documentation: Marissa will add the immediate rollback script to the Drive folder and include the exact CLI command you can run.

If you confirm the 5%/24h canary and the rollback requirements I’ll send a short mutual action plan and escalate to Rishi for approval on the temporary gating and the SOW language note necessary for the trial.

Available for the runbook call at 14:30 ET today.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Variant gating proposal and emergency hold for model update

Thanks — I reviewed the artifacts and the proposed flow. Approve the temporary conservative gating and the emergency hold mechanics for the trial. A couple of compliance notes before we lock the mutual action plan: 

- I’ll need the exact CLI snippet and an audit-log sample that shows who/when the route pin happened (Marissa, please drop into the Drive folder).
- For procurement: we can accept the operational rollback during trial as long as Olive signs the trial addendum (one-page) acknowledging rollback is an operational control and not a permanent SLA change. Priya — I can draft the addendum language.

Marissa — please add the runbook CLI, audit-log example, and the short addendum draft to the Drive folder and ping me when done.

— Rishi
